mainTopic: The one-טפח כפורת, and the source for a סוכה's ten-טפח minimum height
overview: The amud opens by testing רב הונא's teaching that the כפורת was one טפח thick, based on the word ״פני״ (face). Using the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת and a גזירה שוה to the face of יצחק, the גמרא confirms the one-טפח size. A tradition that the כרובים' faces were at least a טפח supports it too. רבי אבהו explains that a כרוב has a child's face, and he defends this against אביי's challenge from יחזקאל. The גמרא then asks how we know a סוכה needs ten טפחים of empty space below the סכך. It answers with a calculation from the בית עולמים and the משכן: the כרובים filled one-third of the height, and their wings, called 'סוככים', were spread just above ten טפחים. This math only works for רבי מאיר, so for רבי יהודה the גמרא says the ten טפחים are a הלכה למשה מסיני, as רב taught about שיעורין, חציצין, and מחיצין. The גמרא challenges that שיעורין come from the פסוק of the seven species and begins explaining it with wheat. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not compare to the giant bird's face?
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a challenge that began on the previous amud (5a). If the כפורת matches a 'face', maybe it matches the huge face of the bird בר יוכני.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Say it is like the face) of the bird בר יוכני!
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a question from the previous page. The גמרא asks: if the כפורת is sized like 'a face', why not the enormous face of the bird בר יוכני?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said 'face' means one טפח. The challenge points out that faces come in many sizes. A very large creature's face would make the כפורת far thicker than one טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: A legendary giant bird with a very large face
The gold cover on top of the Ark
A handbreadth, a basic unit of measurement

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the tail end of a sentence. The words 'ואימא כאפי' ('say it is like the face of') appeared at the end of the previous amud (5a).

phrases.english: of the bird bar Yokhani!
phrases.notes: This finishes the question 'ואימא כאפי...' that started on the previous amud (5a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge to רב הונא's teaching from the previous amud (5a)
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that 'face' means one טפח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Faces vary in size, so 'face' could point to a giant face much larger than a טפח.

steps.title: When unsure, take the smaller amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the giant-face idea with the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת: if you grab a lot, you may end up holding nothing; if you grab a little, you surely hold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grabbed a lot, you did not grab anything. If you grabbed a little, you did grab something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the giant-bird suggestion. When a source is unclear, we take the smaller, safer amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smaller measurement is included in any larger one, so it is certain. The larger measurement has no clear upper limit and is not proven. So the giant face does not set the size.

keyTerms.meaning: If you grab a lot, you hold nothing; a rule that in doubt we take the minimum
A small amount

steps.whyThisMatters: תפשת מרובה לא תפשת is a general rule used all over ש״ס whenever a size or amount is uncertain.

phrases.english: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp anything;
if you grasped a little, you grasped something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to use the giant bird's face
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A large size cannot be proven; only the smaller size is certain.

steps.title: Then why not a tiny bird's face?
steps.stepSummary: Using the same rule, the גמרא asks: if we always take the smaller amount, why not use a little bird's face, which is far smaller than a טפח?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say it is like the face of a bird, which is very small!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the rule around. If we choose the smallest option, a small bird's face should set the measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפשת מועט seems to lead to the smallest possible face. That would make the כפורת much thinner than one טפח, which contradicts רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird, here a small one
Very small

phrases.english: But say it is like the face of a bird
which is very small!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 2 to attack רב הונא from the other side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we always take the minimum, the smallest face (a little bird's) should apply, giving less than a טפח.

steps.title: רב הונא used a גזירה שוה to a human face
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that רב הונא did not just pick any face. He learned ״פני״ from ״פני״: the כפורת verse and the verse about יצחק's face. So the size is a human face, about one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: רב הונא learned it from the word 'face' and the word 'face'. Here it says 'before (the face of) the כפורת', and there it says 'from the face of יצחק his father'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the challenge. He says רב הונא's source is a word-link, a גזירה שוה, to a verse about a person's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״פני״ appears about the כפורת and about יצחק. Linking them tells us which face is meant: a human face, which is about a טפח. That rules out both the giant bird and the tiny bird.

keyTerms.meaning: Derived or learned, here through a גזירה שוה
Face of / before
It is written here... and it is written there; the standard form of a word-link
Learning one verse from another because they share a word

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not measuring a real animal's face. The גזירה שוה tells us which kind of face, a human one, sets the measurement.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
Rav Huna derived it from 'face' and 'face'.
It is written here: 'Before [the face of] the Ark cover',
and it is written there: 'From the face of Isaac his father'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the tiny-bird challenge by naming the exact source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the source: a גזירה שוה rather than an open comparison to any face
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Face' could mean any creature's face, large or small.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה to יצחק's face sets it at a human face, one טפח.

steps.title: Why not link to פני אלהים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we link to יצחק's face and not to the verse ״כראות פני אלהים״, which also uses the word ״פני״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn instead from the 'face above', as it is written: 'like seeing the face of God, and you accepted me'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of verse. Another verse also says ״פני״, about a heavenly face, which may be much larger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה needs the matching word, and ״פני״ appears in several places. So why pick יצחק? A heavenly face would give a different, larger size.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us learn (from elsewhere)
The 'face above', a heavenly face

phrases.english: But let us derive it from the face above,
as it is written: 'As one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which ״פני״ verse the גזירה שוה should use
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of יצחק's face for the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another verse also says ״פני״, so it could be the source instead and give a different size.

steps.title: The same rule rejects the heavenly face
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with תפשת מרובה לא תפשת again. Between a larger heavenly face and a human face, we take the smaller one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grabbed a lot, you did not grab anything. If you grabbed a little, you did grab something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the heavenly-face option. It uses the same 'take the smaller amount' rule from before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses have the word ״פני″, so the link alone cannot decide between them. The tie-breaker is to choose the smaller, certain size, the human face. Here the rule chooses between two possible sources.

keyTerms.meaning: The face of God or a heavenly being, assumed to be large

phrases.english: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp anything;
if you grasped a little, you grasped something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5 with the rule from step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using פני אלהים as the source of the גזירה שוה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It gives a larger size, which is uncertain; the smaller human face is certain.

steps.title: Why not link to the faces of the כרובים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a closer source: the כרובים on top of the כפורת, whose verse also says ״פני″. Their faces were thought to be small.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn instead from the כרוב, as it is written: 'Toward the כפורת shall be the faces of the כרובים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ״פני″ verse, about the כרובים. It is even connected to the כפורת itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרובים sat right on the כפורת, so their verse is a very natural source. If their faces were smaller than a טפח, the rule of taking the minimum would make the כפורת thinner than רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden winged figures on top of the כפורת

phrases.english: But let us derive it from the cherub,
as it is written: 'Toward the Ark cover shall be the faces of the cherubs'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another candidate verse, one that seems to give a smaller size
steps.kashyaTarget: The one-טפח measurement drawn from יצחק's face
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כרובים verse also says ״פני″ and is tied to the כפורת. If their faces were small, the minimum rule would choose them.

steps.title: Tradition: the כרובים' faces were at least a טפח
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב cites a tradition that the כרובים' faces were not smaller than a טפח. So this source also gives one טפח, and רב הונא learned it from here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: We have a tradition that the faces of the כרובים were not less than a טפח. And רב הונא also learned it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the last challenge. The כרובים' faces were at least a טפח, so they do not lower the measurement. In fact they support רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the כרובים had small faces. A received tradition (גמירי) says their faces were at least a טפח, so this verse also gives one טפח. רב הונא's ruling is confirmed by both verses.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (passed down, not derived from a verse)
Smaller than / less than
He learned it from here

steps.whatToRemember: The כפורת was one טפח thick, learned from the word ״פני״ (face). Two rules work together: תפשת מרובה לא תפשת (take the smaller amount), and a גזירה שוה to a face of about one טפח, either יצחק's face or the כרובים' faces, which by tradition were at least a טפח.
steps.whyThisMatters: The one-טפח thickness of the כפורת is the basis for later measurements in the סוגיא. These include the ten-טפחים height of the ארון and כפורת, which helps set the minimum height of a סוכה.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּמִירִי אֵין פְּנֵי כְרוּבִים פְּחוּתִין מִטֶּפַח,
phrases.english: We have a tradition that the faces of the cherubs were not less than a handbreadth,
and Rav Huna also derived it from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמִירִי אֵין פְּנֵי כְרוּבִים פְּחוּתִין מִטֶּפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 and turns the challenge into support for רב הונא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual correction from a tradition: the כרובים' faces were at least a טפח
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כרובים had small faces, which would lower the size below a טפח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כרובים' faces were at least a טפח, so this verse also supports רב הונא's one-טפח measurement.

steps.title: What does a כרוב look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the form of a כרוב's face is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is a כרוב?
steps.whatsHappening: Since we just used the faces of the כרובים to measure one טפח, the גמרא asks a simple question: what did a כרוב's face actually look like? This question sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the כרובים' faces were at least a טפח. That only works if a כרוב has something like a human face. So the גמרא wants to know what kind of face it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A cherub, one of the golden figures on top of the כפורת
And what is...?

phrases.english: And what is a cherub?
phrases.notes: Asks about the shape of its face.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the כרובים mentioned in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The form or appearance of a כרוב's face.

steps.title: A כרוב has a child's face
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that כרוב means 'like a child', based on the Babylonian word for child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: כרוב means 'כ-רביא', like a child. In בבל, people call a child 'רביא'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that a כרוב has the face of a young child. He shows this by breaking the word כרוב into 'כ' (like) and 'רביא' (child).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a word-play explanation. The letter כ means 'like', and the rest of the word sounds like 'רביא', the Babylonian word for a little child. So a כרוב has a small human face, which fits the idea that its face is about a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a child (כ = like, רביא = child)
A baby or young child
Babylonia, where people used the word רביא for a child

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: like a child,
for in Babylonia they call a child 'ravya'.
phrases.notes: The word כרוב is being split into כ plus רוב, which sounds like רביא, a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כרוב has the face of a young child.

steps.title: אביי: Then a כרוב and an אדם would be the same
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבי אבהו from a פסוק in יחזקאל that lists a כרוב's face and a man's face as two different faces.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, what about the פסוק 'The face of the first was the face of the כרוב, and the face of the second was the face of a man'? Then the כרוב is the same as the man!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבי אבהו's explanation. A פסוק lists 'face of a כרוב' and 'face of a man' as two separate faces. If a כרוב is just a human child, why are they listed separately?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל's vision, each face is supposed to be different. If a כרוב's face is human, it seems to repeat the man's face. So אביי argues that a כרוב cannot simply be a human face.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so... (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
That is the same as
The face of a man

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if so,
that which is written: 'The face of the first was the face of the cherub,
and the face of the second was the face of a man',
then the cherub is the same as the man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's definition from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that a כרוב has a human child's face.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק treats a כרוב's face and a man's face as two different faces, so a כרוב cannot simply be a human face.

steps.title: A big face and a small face
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both are human faces. The אדם is a big adult face and the כרוב is a small child's face.
steps.simpleTranslation: A big face and a small face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבהו. Both faces are human, but they are still different. The 'man' is an adult face and the 'כרוב' is a child's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two human faces can still count as separate faces in the vision if one is grown-up and one is young. So the פסוק has no repetition, and רבי אבהו's explanation stands. This is a side discussion about the כרובים. The one-טפח size of their faces rests on the tradition (גמירי) in step 8, not on this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A big face (an adult's)
A small face (a child's)

steps.whatToRemember: A כרוב has a small, child-like human face. The one-טפח size of their faces comes from the tradition in step 8, not from this point.

phrases.english: A large face and a small face.
phrases.notes: The man's face is the grown-up one, and the כרוב's face is the child's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: both are human faces, but of different sizes and ages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A human כרוב face would be identical to the 'face of a man' in the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man's face is an adult's and the כרוב's face is a child's, so they are distinct.

steps.title: Maybe the ten טפחים include the סכך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source from the ארון: its ten טפחים include the כפורת on top, so maybe a סוכה's ten should include the סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that the empty space of the סוכה must be ten טפחים without its סכך? Say it is ten together with its סכך!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא goes back to the halacha of סוכה and raises a new problem with learning from the ארון. A סוכה needs ten טפחים of empty space under the סכך. But the ארון's ten includes its lid, so maybe the סוכה's ten should include the סכך too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון was nine טפחים and the כפורת was one, which makes ten in total. If the סוכה copies the ארון, the 'roof' (סכך) should be counted inside the ten, just as the כפורת is. That would make a lower סוכה כשר, which goes against the rule that the inside space itself must be ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Its empty inside space
Its סכך, the roof covering of the סוכה
Without, not counting
Together with

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the כרובים anymore. The גמרא has returned to the main topic: the ten-טפח height of a סוכה.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that its inside space is ten without its roofing?
Say it is ten together with its roofing!
phrases.notes: Just like the ten of the ארון counts its cover, the כפורת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the side point on the כרובים, the גמרא tests whether the ארון source really proves the סוכה rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of the סוכה's ten טפחים from the ארון and כפורת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ארון's ten טפחים include its cover, so the parallel would count the סכך inside the ten instead of requiring ten of empty space.

steps.title: A new source: the measurements of the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches sources and learns the סוכה's height from the בית עולמים, citing the house's thirty-אמה height and the כרובים' ten-אמה height.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learned it from the בית עולמים, as it says: 'The house that King שלמה built for ה׳ was sixty אמות long, twenty wide, and thirty אמות high.' And it says: 'The height of one כרוב was ten אמות, and so was the second כרוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the problem in step 13, the גמרא gives a different source for the ten טפחים: the בית המקדש that שלמה built. It quotes two פסוקים: the house was thirty אמות high and the כרובים were ten אמות high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put these two numbers together and the כרובים in שלמה's בית המקדש filled exactly one-third of the height (10 out of 30). This ratio is the key that will be applied to the משכן in the next steps. The idea is that the space under the כרובים' wings works like the empty space under the סכך, so the סכך is not counted.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'eternal house', the permanent בית המקדש built by שלמה
He learned it (derived it)
Its height
A cubit, equal to six טפחים

phrases.english: Rather, he derived it from the eternal Temple,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה לַה׳
phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the house which King Solomon built for the Lord,
its length was sixty cubits, and its breadth twenty,
and its height thirty cubits'.
And it is written: 'The height of the first cherub was ten cubits,
and likewise the second cherub',

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 13 by replacing the ארון source with a source from the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of source: the derivation moves from the ארון to the בית עולמים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוכה's ten טפחים are learned from the ארון, which would include the cover.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ten טפחים are learned from the proportions of the כרובים in the בית המקדש, which point to empty space under the cover.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new source is what gives us the halacha that a סוכה needs ten טפחים of empty space, not counting the סכך.

steps.title: ברייתא: The same one-third ratio applies in the משכן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that just as the כרובים filled one-third of the height in the בית עולמים, they also filled one-third of the height in the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: Just as we find in the בית עולמים that the כרובים stood at one-third of the house, so in the משכן too, the כרובים stood at one-third of the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the new source. It takes the one-third ratio from שלמה's בית המקדש and applies it to the משכן. This sets up the measurements that will be worked out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים gave numbers only for שלמה's בית המקדש. The ברייתא says the same proportion was true in the משכן, whose height was ten אמות. Applying one-third to the משכן's height gives the measurements of the ארון and the כרובים in טפחים, which lead to the סוכה rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא teaches
Just as we find... (introduces a comparison)
One-third of the height of the house
The portable Tabernacle in the desert

steps.whatToRemember: The סוכה's ten טפחים of empty space are now learned from the כרובים, who filled one-third of the height in both the בית המקדש and the משכן.

phrases.english: And it is taught: Just as we find in the eternal Temple
that the cherubs stand at one-third of the house,
in the Tabernacle as well,
the cherubs stand at one-third of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14 by carrying the one-third ratio from the בית עולמים over to the משכן.
steps.raayaObject: The derivation of the סוכה's height from the proportions of the כרובים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the כרובים filled one-third of the height in both the בית עולמים and the משכן.

steps.title: The math that puts the wings exactly ten טפחים above the כפורת
steps.stepSummary: The משכן was ten אמות tall, which is sixty טפחים. A third of that is twenty טפחים. Take away the ten טפחים of the ארון and כפורת, and ten טפחים are left for the כרובים. The תורה calls their wings 'סוככים', so 'סכך' is ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall was the משכן? Ten אמות, because the פסוק says each board was ten אמות long. How many טפחים is that? Sixty. A third of it is twenty. Subtract the ten טפחים of the ארון and כפורת, and ten are left. The פסוק says the כרובים spread their wings upward, 'covering' the כפורת. So the תורה called it 'סכך' when it was ten טפחים above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא from the last step to do the actual math. The result is that the כרובים' covering wings were ten טפחים above the כפורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the כרובים filled one-third of the height, just as in the בית עולמים. The משכן's height is known from the boards, so a third of it is twenty טפחים. The ארון and כפורת take up ten of those twenty, which leaves ten for the כרובים. Since the תורה uses the word 'סוככים' for their wings, we learn that 'סכך' means a covering at least ten טפחים high.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle in the desert
A wall-board of the משכן; it was ten אמות long, which gives the משכן's height
Handbreadths (Aramaic for טפחים)
Subtract, take away
Covering or sheltering; the same root as סכך and סוכה
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the Author of the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source in this סוגיא for why a סוכה must be at least ten טפחים tall.

phrases.english: How tall was the Tabernacle? Ten cubits,
as it is written: 'Ten cubits is the length of a board',
phrases.notes: The boards stood upright, so their length is the height of the משכן.

phrases.english: How much is that? Sixty handbreadths,
phrases.notes: Ten אמות, at six טפחים each.

phrases.english: one third of it is how much? Twenty handbreadths,
subtract the ten of the Ark and the Ark cover,
phrases.notes: The ארון was nine טפחים and the כפורת one טפח, as the גמרא said earlier.

phrases.english: ten remain,
and it is written: 'And the cherubs shall spread their wings upward
covering the Ark cover with their wings',
the Merciful One called it 'covering'
above ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא in Step 15 to do the math for the משכן.
steps.raayaObject: That a סוכה's סכך must be at least ten טפחים high
steps.raayaSupportSource: The board-length פסוק, the one-third ratio from the ברייתא, and the word 'סוככים' in the פסוק about the כרובים

steps.title: Maybe the wings were level with the כרובים' heads
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the wings were above the כרובים' heads. Maybe they were at head level, so the ten טפחים would include the wings themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that their wings were above their heads? Maybe they were level with their heads!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the math. It is not clear exactly where the wings were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten טפחים are the height of the כרובים' bodies. If the wings were level with their heads, the 'סכך' would sit inside those ten טפחים, and the space under it would be less than ten. The proof only works if the wings were above the ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Wings
Above their heads
Level with their heads

phrases.english: From where do we know that their wings
stood above their heads?
Perhaps they stood level with their heads!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the proof in Step 16 places the wings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the wings, the 'סכך', were above the ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wings were at head level, the ten טפחים include the covering, so the space underneath is less than ten.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'upward'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that the פסוק says the wings were spread 'למעלה', so they were above the כרובים' heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It is written 'upward'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question with one word from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פורשי כנפים למעלה' tells us the wings rose above the כרובים' bodies. So the ten טפחים are open space under the wings, and that saves the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Upward, above
An אמורא who answers the question here

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
'Upward' is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wings might have been at head level.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'למעלה' shows the wings were above the heads.

steps.title: Maybe the wings were very high
steps.stepSummary: If 'למעלה' means above, maybe it means far above. Then we could not get an exact ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say that they were raised very high?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. 'Upward' could mean far upward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wings were far above the heads, the 'סכך' would be at some unknown height above ten. Then the פסוק would not teach a ten-טפחים rule at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised up
A lot, very much

phrases.english: But say that they were raised very high?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'למעלה' as just slightly above the heads
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Upward' does not say how far up, so the height of the 'סכך' would be unknown.

steps.title: 'Upward' is written only once
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק does not say 'למעלה למעלה', so it means only a little above the heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'upward, upward'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a question: the פסוק says 'upward' only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One 'למעלה' means just above the heads, not far above. So the 'סכך' was right above the ten טפחים, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (a question that means 'it is not written')

steps.whatToRemember: The כרובים' wings were just above their ten-טפח bodies. The תורה called them 'סוככים', so a סוכה must have at least ten טפחים of space under the סכך.

phrases.english: Is it written 'upward, upward'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wings might have been very high.
steps.terutzMaskana: A single 'למעלה' means just above the heads.

steps.title: This works for רבי מאיר, but what about רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The math assumed every אמה is six טפחים, which is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says the אמה used for כלים is only five טפחים. Then the math changes.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי מאיר, who said all the אמות were medium-sized. But according to רבי יהודה, who said a building אמה is six טפחים and a vessel אמה is five, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. The next step does the actual math to show the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון is a כלי, not a building. If its אמה is only five טפחים, the ארון is shorter than we thought, and the space left for the כרובים changes. The משכן itself is a building, so its sixty טפחים stay the same.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one view, but not for another)
Medium-sized: an אמה of six טפחים
The אמה used to measure a building
Vessels, such as the ארון
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Meir,
who said: all the cubits were medium-sized.
But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
a cubit of a building is six handbreadths,
and that of vessels is five,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the wording of the פסוק is settled, the גמרא challenges the measurements behind the proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The math assumed six-טפח אמות for the ארון. Under רבי יהודה it is five, so the numbers change.

steps.title: By רבי יהודה's math, a סוכה would need eleven and a half טפחים
steps.stepSummary: By רבי יהודה, the ארון and כפורת are eight and a half טפחים. Twenty minus eight and a half leaves eleven and a half, so a סוכה should need eleven and a half טפחים, which no one holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall are the ארון and כפורת? Eight and a half. That leaves eleven and a half. So say a סוכה must be eleven and a half טפחים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math to show the problem with the proof under רבי יהודה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון was one and a half אמות, which is seven and a half טפחים using five-טפח אמות. Add the one-טפח כפורת and you get eight and a half. Subtract that from twenty and you get eleven and a half for the כרובים. So the proof would give a minimum height that no one actually holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight and a half
Eleven
Remain, are left over

steps.confusionAlert: Only the ארון, a כלי, shrinks to five-טפח אמות. The משכן is a building, so it stays at sixty טפחים, and a third of it is still twenty.

phrases.english: How much are the Ark and Ark cover?
Eight and a half,
phrases.notes: 1.5 אמות × 5 = 7.5 טפחים, plus a one-טפח כפורת.

phrases.english: eleven and a half remain,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא סוּכָּה עַד דְּהָוְיָא חַד סְרֵי וּפַלְגָא!
phrases.english: so say a sukka is not valid until it is eleven and a half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge opened in Step 21 by doing the math.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ten-טפחים source under רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With five-טפח אמות for the ארון, the space left is eleven and a half טפחים, so the proof gives a minimum that no one accepts.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, the ten טפחים are a tradition from סיני
steps.stepSummary: The calculation from the כרובים fails for רבי יהודה. So the גמרא says that according to him, the ten טפחים of a סוכה were learned as a received tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, according to רבי יהודה, they learned it as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on deriving ten טפחים from the ארון and כרובים according to רבי יהודה. Instead, it says he knows the number from a הלכה received at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that with a five-טפח אמה, the math gives eleven and a half טפחים, which no one holds. The word אלא signals that the גמרא is dropping the old path for רבי יהודה. It does not fix the math. It replaces the source entirely. The derivation from the כרובים still works for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals a switch to a new approach after the old one failed.
A received law (here, a הלכה למשה מסיני)
They learned it by tradition

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
they learned it as a received law (from Sinai).
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rule that a סוכה must be at least ten טפחים high.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 21–22 by replacing the source for רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of source: tradition instead of a derivation from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ten טפחים must come from the measurements of the ארון, כפורת, and כרובים for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, the ten טפחים come from a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: רב's statement: measures, interpositions, and partitions are from Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from רב that שיעורין, חציצין, and מחיצין are all הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: measures, interpositions, and partitions are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that such a tradition exists. It quotes רב, who lists three areas of הלכה that were given orally at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's list includes שיעורין (amounts like a כזית), חציצין (barriers that invalidate a טבילה), and מחיצין (rules of halachic walls). The ten-טפח height of a סוכה fits into this group of oral measurements. That is the support for step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Halachic measures, such as a כַּזַּיִת or a כְּבֵיצָה
Interpositions: things that block water from the body during טבילה
Partitions: the halachic rules of walls
A law given orally to משה at סיני, not written in the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's principle is a famous foundation. Many basic measurements in הלכה are oral tradition rather than derived from a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
Measures, interpositions, and partitions —
are a law given to Moshe at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in step 23
steps.raayaObject: That the ten-טפח minimum can be a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב, quoted by רבי חייא בר אשי

steps.title: Challenge: measures are hinted to in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: שיעורין seem to come from the תורה, because רב חנין says the whole פסוק 'ארץ חטה ושעורה...' was said to teach measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Measures are from the Torah! As it is written, 'A land of wheat and barley and vines and figs and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,' and רב חנין said: this entire פסוק was said to teach measures!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first item on רב's list, שיעורין. רב חנין says the seven foods in this פסוק are the source for measures, so how can שיעורין be only an oral tradition?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה itself hints to שיעורין, then calling them הלכה למשה מסיני looks wrong. The challenge does not attack מחיצין or חציצין. It targets only שיעורין. Right after this, the גמרא will start showing how each food in the פסוק teaches a measure.

keyTerms.meaning: From the תורה (written)
They are
It was said in order to teach measures

phrases.english: Measures are from the Torah!
As it is written: 'A land of wheat and barley
and vines and figs and pomegranates,
a land of olive oil and honey' (Devarim 8:8),
and Rav Chanin said:
This entire verse was stated for measures!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement brought in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that שיעורין are a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חנין shows the Torah hints to שיעורין in a פסוק, so they are not purely an oral tradition.

steps.title: Wheat teaches the measure for a house with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining רב חנין: חטה teaches a measure for a בית המנוגע. It quotes a משנה about a person who enters such a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wheat is for a house with צרעת, as we learned: One who enters a house with צרעת with his garments on his shoulders and his sandals and rings in his hand, he and they become טמא immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to show how each food in the פסוק teaches a measure, beginning with wheat. This is a setup: the משנה quoted here is only the first part, and the actual wheat measure comes in the next lines (on the next amud).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first sets up the basic case. Someone who walks into a בית המנוגע carrying his things, not wearing them, becomes טמא right away together with those things. The continuation of the משנה (not yet on this amud) contrasts someone who is dressed. His clothes become טמא only after he stays long enough to eat a meal-sized portion of wheat bread. That is where חטה gives a measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A house afflicted with צָרַעַת (ויקרא פרק יד)
As we learned in a מִשְׁנָה
Here: his garments (not 'utensils')
They become טמא immediately

steps.confusionAlert: Here כליו means his clothes, not utensils. The point is that the clothes are carried on his shoulders, not worn. That is why they become טמא at once, without any time measure.

phrases.english: Wheat — for a house afflicted with tzara'as,
as we learned: One who enters a house afflicted with tzara'as
with his garments on his shoulders,
and his sandals and rings in his hand —
he and they are impure immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins spelling out רב חנין's claim from step 25, item by item
steps.raayaObject: רב חנין's claim that the פסוק teaches שיעורין (starting with חטה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about entering a בית המנוגע (continued on the next amud)
